caseTitle.zh: 加護病房的第一次坐起

condition.zh: 重症復健 · 早期活動

title.en: A rehab day in the ICU

tagline.zh: 呼吸器旁的白板、一塊溝通板和床緣的三分鐘
tagline.en: A whiteboard by the ventilator, a communication board and three minutes on the edge of the bed

desc.zh: 跟著周主治進加護病房：安全篩檢、影像、家屬會談、夜裡一通譫妄的電話。病人搖頭說不要的時候，下一句話是你的。
desc.en: Into the ICU with Dr Chou: the safety screen, the images, the family meeting, a night call about delirium. When the patient shakes her head, the next sentence is yours.

desc.zh: 關節活動度、床緣坐起、監視器的位置和停止手勢都在你手上；她第一次坐起來的那三分鐘，你撐著。
desc.en: Range of motion, sitting on the edge of the bed, where the monitor is and the stop signal are yours; for her first three minutes sitting up, you are the support.

about.zh: 腰上永遠掛著計步器。進加護病房前會先把咖啡放在門口的櫃子上，出來的時候涼了。
about.en: Always a pedometer on his belt. Leaves his coffee on the cabinet by the ICU door; it is cold when he comes out.

about.zh: 7 床的主責護理師。管路的長度她用眼睛量。她說：要動可以，先問我。
about.en: Primary nurse for bed 7. Measures line lengths by eye. Her rule: you can move her, but ask me first.

about.zh: 坐起的時候他的手永遠在氣切管上。口頭禪：管子不動，人才能動。
about.en: During a sit-up his hand never leaves the tracheostomy. Motto: the tube stays still so the person can move.

about.zh: 隨身帶一本溝通圖卡，加護病房多帶一塊白板。她說：一次問一個問題。
about.en: Carries a book of picture cards, plus a whiteboard for the ICU. Her rule: one question at a time.

role.zh: 敗血症第九天，氣切，清醒
role.en: Day nine of sepsis, tracheostomy, awake

about.zh: 虛構教學個案。六十二歲，國小退休老師，肺炎變敗血症住進來。醒了，說不出話，眼睛很忙。
about.en: Fictional teaching case. Sixty-two, a retired primary-school teacher, admitted when pneumonia became sepsis. Awake, voiceless, eyes very busy.

about.zh: 每天會客時間提早半小時到門口。帶著她的老花眼鏡和一本她的日記。
about.en: At the door half an hour before every visiting slot. Brings her reading glasses and her diary.

about.zh: 講話很快，但會等你複誦。他的目標板永遠比你的早寫好。
about.en: Talks fast but waits for your read-back. His goal board is always written before yours.

plain.zh: 重症病人一穩定就開始動：翻身、坐起、床緣、站立、走。躺越久，肌肉掉越快。
plain.en: Getting a critically ill person moving as soon as they are stable: turning, sitting, the edge of the bed, standing, walking. The longer they lie, the faster muscle disappears.

plain.zh: 重症、臥床、發炎與鎮靜合在一起，讓全身肌肉在幾天內變弱。醒來時連抬手都重。
plain.en: Critical illness, bed rest, inflammation and sedation together weaken muscles all over the body within days. On waking, even lifting an arm is heavy.

plain.zh: 在頸部氣管開一個小口放管子呼吸。空氣不經過聲帶，所以說不出聲音，但聽得懂、想得清楚。
plain.en: A small opening in the windpipe at the neck with a tube to breathe through. Air bypasses the vocal cords, so there is no voice, but hearing and thinking are intact.

plain.zh: 一步一步減少呼吸器的幫忙，直到病人自己呼吸。坐起來、肺底張開，是脫離的好朋友。
plain.en: Reducing the ventilator's help step by step until the person breathes alone. Sitting up and opening the lung bases is weaning's best friend.

plain.zh: 寫字板或圖卡，讓不能說話的人指、寫、點頭。一次一個問題，等她答完。
plain.en: A writing board or picture cards so a voiceless person can point, write and nod. One question at a time; wait for the answer.

plain.zh: 活動前跟病人約好的手勢，例如舉手。她一比，全隊就停。不能說話的人也要有否決權。
plain.en: A gesture agreed before the session, such as a raised hand. When she makes it, the whole team stops. A person without a voice still gets a veto.

plain.zh: 指夾或耳夾讀出的血液帶氧比例。坐起時掉下來，先看人、看管路，再看數字。
plain.en: The finger- or ear-clip reading of how much oxygen the blood carries. If it drops as she sits, look at the person and the tubing before the number.

plain.zh: 肺的一部分沒有張開，常在躺久的人的肺底。X 光上變白。坐直、深呼吸、咳痰可以把它打開。
plain.en: Part of the lung not inflated, usually at the bases of someone who has lain for days. It looks white on X-ray. Sitting upright, deep breaths and coughing open it up.

plain.zh: 急性的意識混亂，時好時壞，夜裡最明顯：拔管路、認不得人、或是安靜得不對勁。先找原因，不是先綁。
plain.en: Acute, fluctuating confusion, worst at night: pulling at lines, not recognising people, or an unusual quietness. Find the cause first; restraints are not the first answer.

plain.zh: 用束帶限制病人的手腳。它是最後手段，有醫囑、有時限、有定時檢查，而且要先試過所有不綁的方法。
plain.en: Straps limiting a patient's limbs. A last resort, with an order, a time limit and regular checks, and only after every non-restraint option has been tried.

plain.zh: 家人和團隊幫病人寫下每天發生的事。出院後讀，可以把斷掉的記憶接回來，減少惡夢。
plain.en: Family and staff write down what happens each day. Read after discharge, it stitches broken memories back together and reduces nightmares.

plain.zh: 離開加護病房後留下的虛弱、記憶問題、焦慮與惡夢。復健從加護病房就開始，就是為了它。
plain.en: The weakness, memory problems, anxiety and nightmares that linger after intensive care. Rehabilitation starts in the ICU precisely because of it.

plain.zh: 關節能彎到、伸到哪裡。躺久的腳踝最先變緊，每天量，每天動。
plain.en: How far a joint bends and straightens. Ankles stiffen first in someone who has lain for days; measure daily, move daily.

text.zh: 管路有長度，病人有重心。坐起前把管路理順，呼吸治療師的手放在氣切上。設定是重症團隊的事，不是復健的事。
text.en: The tubing has a length and the patient has a centre of gravity. Tidy the circuit before she sits and keep the respiratory therapist's hand on the tracheostomy. Settings belong to the intensive-care team, not to rehab.

text.zh: 坐起前先轉到你看得到的角度，警報音量開著。數字掉下來，先看人，再看它。
text.en: Turn it to where you can see it before the sit-up and keep the alarm audible. When a number drops, look at the person first, then at it.

text.zh: 白板、筆、圖卡、字母表。眼鏡先戴上。一次一個問題，等她寫完再問下一個。
text.en: Whiteboard, pen, picture cards, an alphabet chart. Glasses on first. One question at a time; wait until she finishes writing.

text.zh: 床頭可以搖高、可以變椅子。坐到床緣以前，先讓床做一半的工作。
text.en: The head rises and the bed turns into a chair. Before she sits on the edge, let the bed do half the work.

text.zh: 呼吸、鎮靜、活動、家屬，四格。活動那一格寫「床緣坐三分鐘」，比寫「復健」有用。
text.en: Breathing, sedation, mobility, family: four boxes. “Three minutes on the edge of the bed” in the mobility box beats “physio”.

name.en: The first word on the board

text.zh: 阿玉姨坐起來之後寫的。歪歪的一個「謝」。阿玲拍了照，貼在目標板旁邊。
text.en: Written by Auntie Yu after she sat up. A wobbly “thanks”. Ling photographed it and stuck it next to the goal board.

text.zh: 動之前問四個系統：意識（清醒、能遵從指令）、呼吸（氧氣需求與呼吸器設定穩定，依團隊標準）、循環（血壓心跳穩定，沒有新的升壓需求）、管路（氣切、點滴、尿管固定且長度足夠）。再加一個人：團隊分工與停止訊號。篩檢過了不代表不會出事，而是出事時每個人知道自己該做什麼。
text.en: Before moving anyone, ask four systems: consciousness (awake, follows commands), breathing (oxygen need and ventilator settings stable, by the team's criteria), circulation (blood pressure and heart rate stable, no new vasopressor need), lines (tracheostomy, drips and catheter secured and long enough). Then add the people: team roles and a stop signal. Passing the screen does not mean nothing will happen; it means everyone knows what to do when it does.

text.zh: 氣切病人的空氣不過聲帶，所以沒有聲音，但大腦清清楚楚。對著她說話，不是對著家屬；眼鏡戴上、助聽器戴上；一次一個問題、能點頭回答的先問；給她時間寫。清醒的病人，自己的活動自己同意，家屬的同意不能替代她的搖頭。
text.en: A tracheostomy sends air past the vocal cords, so there is no voice, but the mind is clear. Talk to her, not to her family; glasses on, hearing aid in; one question at a time, yes-or-no questions first; give her time to write. An awake patient consents to her own session; a relative's yes does not overrule her shake of the head.

name.zh: 譫妄：先找原因再談約束

text.zh: 夜裡拔管路的病人，先問：痛嗎、尿脹嗎、缺氧嗎、便秘嗎、哪一種藥剛加的、睡了幾小時。然後做不用藥的事：眼鏡助聽器、開一點燈、報時間地點、家人的聲音、白天坐起夜裡關燈、減少不必要的警報。約束是最後手段：有醫囑、有時限、定時鬆開檢查皮膚。綁住一個害怕的人，通常讓他更害怕。
text.en: For the patient pulling at lines at night, ask first: pain, a full bladder, low oxygen, constipation, which drug was just added, how many hours of sleep. Then do the non-drug things: glasses and hearing aid, a little light, the time and place said aloud, a family voice, sitting up by day and lights off by night, fewer needless alarms. Restraints are the last resort: ordered, time-limited, released regularly to check the skin. Tying down a frightened person usually frightens them more.

lines.zh: 加護病房早上八點。警報聲此起彼落，周主治的咖啡留在門口的櫃子上。
lines.en: The ICU at eight in the morning. Alarms answer one another; Dr Chou's coffee stays on the cabinet by the door.

lines.zh: 7 床阿玉姨，肺炎併敗血症第九天，氣切，鎮靜停了兩天，清醒、能遵從指令。四肢都很弱。
lines.en: Bed 7, Auntie Yu, day nine of pneumonia with sepsis, tracheostomy, sedation off for two days, awake and following commands. Weak in all four limbs.

lines.zh: 加護病房肌無力。會走路出去的病人，都是從會坐起來開始的。今天目標？
lines.en: ICU-acquired weakness. Every patient who walks out of here started by sitting up. Today's goal?

lines.zh: 床緣坐起。先過安全篩檢。
lines.en: Sitting on the edge of the bed. Safety screen first.

guide.en: Run the safety screen with Ling

lines.zh: 要動可以，先跟我過一遍。你說順序。
lines.en: You can move her, but walk it through with me first. Give me the order.

q.zh: 早期活動前的安全篩檢順序
q.en: The safety screen before early mobilisation

steps.zh: 呼吸：氧氣需求與呼吸器設定穩定
steps.en: Breathing: oxygen need and ventilator settings stable

steps.zh: 循環：血壓心跳穩定，無新升壓需求
steps.en: Circulation: pressure and rate stable, no new vasopressor

steps.zh: 管路：氣切、點滴、尿管固定夠長
steps.en: Lines: tracheostomy, drips, catheter secured and long enough

steps.zh: 團隊：分工、停止訊號、誰顧氣切
steps.en: Team: roles, the stop signal, who holds the tracheostomy

post.zh: 過了。氣切阿強顧，管路我顧，監視器你們顧。
post.en: Passed. Chiang holds the tracheostomy, I hold the lines, you two watch the monitor.

post.zh: 篩檢過了不代表不會出事，是出事時每個人知道自己該做什麼。
post.en: Passing the screen does not mean nothing will happen. It means everyone knows their job when it does.

note.en: The board, the joints, a shake of the head

lines.zh: 阿玉姨眼睛睜著，嘴唇動了幾下，沒有聲音。她先生站在床尾。
lines.en: Auntie Yu's eyes are open; her lips move, soundlessly. Her husband stands at the foot of the bed.

lines.zh: 她說她很累。我替她講就好。
lines.en: She says she's tired. I can speak for her.

lines.zh: 先生，謝謝。不過我想聽她自己說。眼鏡帶來了嗎？
lines.en: Thank you, sir. But I'd like to hear it from her. Did you bring her glasses?

lines.zh: 阿玉姨，我一次問一個問題，您點頭或搖頭就好。
lines.en: Auntie Yu, I'll ask one question at a time; a nod or a shake is enough.

guide.zh: 和黃語言治療師設溝通板
guide.en: Set up the board with Huang

lines.zh: 氣切沒有聲音，不是沒有話。這題寫的是失語症，但原則一樣：說不出不代表聽不懂。
lines.en: A tracheostomy takes the voice, not the words. This exercise is written for aphasia, but the principle is the same: voiceless is not mindless.

post.zh: 眼鏡戴上、白板給她、等她寫完。她第一句寫的是：「怕掉下去」。
post.en: Glasses on, board in her hand, wait for her to finish. Her first line: “afraid of falling”.

guide.zh: 量阿玉姨的關節活動度
guide.en: Measure Auntie Yu's range of motion

lines.zh: 躺九天的關節。量角器，膝蓋、腳踝都量，寫在目標板。
lines.en: Nine days of lying down. Goniometer: knee and ankle, written on the goal board.

post.zh: 關節活動度今天是起點，不是成績。明天同一個人再量。
post.en: Today's range of motion is the starting line, not a score. Same person measures tomorrow.

guide.zh: 問阿玉姨願不願意坐起
guide.en: Ask Auntie Yu about sitting up

lines.zh: 阿玉姨，下午我們想讓您坐到床邊。好嗎？
lines.en: Auntie Yu, this afternoon we'd like you to sit on the edge of the bed. All right?

lines.zh: 她搖頭。慢慢地、很確定地搖頭。
lines.en: She shakes her head. Slowly, and very certainly.

lines.zh: 我同意就好了，她需要動。
lines.en: I'll agree for her. She needs to move.

q.zh: 清醒的病人搖頭。你怎麼做？
q.en: An awake patient shakes her head. What do you do?

options.zh: 問她怕什麼，說明步驟，約定停止手勢，再問一次
options.en: Ask what she fears, explain the steps, agree a stop signal, ask again

why.zh: 她寫過「怕掉下去」。先處理害怕，給她否決權，同意才會是真的。
why.en: She wrote “afraid of falling”. Deal with the fear, give her a veto, and the yes will be real.

options.en: Her husband agreed; go ahead as planned

why.zh: 清醒的病人自己決定。家屬的同意不能替代她的搖頭。
why.en: An awake patient decides for herself. A relative's yes does not overrule her shake of the head.

why.zh: 尊重拒絕沒有錯，但沒問原因就跳過，明天還是搖頭，肌肉又少一天。
why.en: Respecting a refusal is right, but skipping without asking why means another shake tomorrow and one more day of muscle lost.

post.zh: 她寫了：「有人扶，可以。舉手就停。」
post.en: She wrote: “If someone holds me, yes. Hand up means stop.”

post.zh: 停止手勢，舉手。全隊記住。
post.en: Stop signal: a raised hand. Whole team, remember it.

note.zh: 胸片：肺底白白的；坐起來的理由
note.en: Chest film: white bases; the reason to sit up

sub.zh: 7 床十一點做自主呼吸試驗，活動排後面
sub.en: Bed 7 has a breathing trial at eleven; mobilise after

lines.zh: 7 床十一點做呼吸器脫離的自主呼吸試驗，別跟你們撞在一起。試驗完、休息過，下午再坐。可以？
lines.en: Bed 7 has her weaning breathing trial at eleven; don't collide with it. After the trial and a rest, sit her up this afternoon. Agreed?

lines.zh: 複誦：十一點自主呼吸試驗，下午一點半床緣坐起，呼吸治療師在場。
lines.en: Read-back: breathing trial at eleven, edge-of-bed sit at half past one, respiratory therapist present.

lines.zh: 對。還有，她先生在門口問了三次她什麼時候能說話。你們幫我回答一次。
lines.en: Right. And her husband has asked at the door three times when she will speak. Answer him once for me.

guide.en: The chest film at the workstation

lines.zh: 今天早上的片子。你看肺底。
lines.en: This morning's film. Look at the bases.

lines.zh: 問題：這張片子告訴你，坐起來會幫什麼忙？
lines.en: The question: what does this film say sitting up will do for her?

question.zh: 氣切病人躺九天，胸片雙下肺變白。坐起來為什麼有幫助？
question.en: Nine days supine with a tracheostomy, white lower zones on the film. Why does sitting up help?

answer.zh: 雙下肺變白多半是肺塌陷加分泌物堆積。直立時橫膈下降、肺底張開、痰比較咳得出來，氧合改善，呼吸器脫離也容易。先確認氣切管位置正常、沒有氣胸，再動。
answer.en: White lower zones here are mostly atelectasis plus pooled secretions. Upright, the diaphragm drops, the bases open, secretions clear more easily, oxygenation improves and weaning gets easier. Check first that the tracheostomy tube sits normally and there is no pneumothorax, then move.

post.zh: 坐起之前我先抽痰。管子不動，人才能動。
post.en: I'll suction before she sits. The tube stays still so the person can move.

note.zh: 坐起三分鐘；血氧掉了一次

lines.zh: 坐起時你的眼睛要同時看得到她的臉和監視器。先找到它。
lines.en: During the sit-up your eyes must hold her face and the monitor at once. Find it first.

q.zh: 找到床邊監視器，轉到你看得到的角度
q.en: Find the bedside monitor and turn it to face you

post.zh: 警報音量開著。管路我理好了，夠長。
post.en: Alarm volume is up. Lines tidied; there's enough slack.

guide.en: Help Auntie Yu to the edge of the bed

lines.zh: 床頭先搖高，兩個人扶，阿強的手在氣切上。她坐到床緣，腳垂下來，眼睛很大。
lines.en: Head of the bed up first, two people supporting, Chiang's hand on the tracheostomy. She reaches the edge, legs dangling, eyes wide.

lines.zh: 阿玉姨，您坐起來了。看著我，慢慢呼吸。
lines.en: Auntie Yu, you're sitting. Look at me and breathe slowly.

lines.zh: 一分鐘後，監視器的聲音變了。血氧往下掉。
lines.en: A minute in, the monitor's tone changes. The oxygen saturation is falling.

options.zh: 停下、扶穩、靠回床頭，呼吸治療師看管路抽痰
options.en: Stop, support her, recline onto the bed, RT checks the circuit and suctions

why.zh: 先看人、看管路：氣切有沒有移位、有沒有痰。靠回去不等於失敗。
why.en: Person and tubing first: has the tracheostomy shifted, is there sputum. Reclining is not failure.

options.zh: 繼續坐，數字等一下會回來
options.en: Keep sitting; the number will come back

why.zh: 數字在掉的時候，不是賭的時候。
why.en: A falling number is not the moment to gamble.

options.zh: 馬上躺平，氧氣開到最大
options.en: Lie her flat at once and turn the oxygen right up

why.zh: 躺平讓肺底更塌；呼吸器設定是重症團隊的事，不是扶人的手去轉的。
why.en: Flat collapses the bases further; ventilator settings belong to the intensive-care team, not to the hands holding her.

post.zh: 一口痰。抽完了，數字回來了。管子沒動。
post.en: A plug of sputum. Suctioned; the number is back. Tube never moved.

lines.zh: 她點頭。第二次坐了三分鐘。到第三分鐘，她舉手。全隊停。
lines.en: She nods. The second sit lasts three minutes. At the third minute she raises her hand. The whole team stops.

lines.zh: 停止手勢有用。她知道自己能喊停，所以敢坐。
lines.en: The stop signal worked. She dared to sit because she knew she could stop it.

lines.zh: 躺回去以後，她在白板上寫了一個歪歪的字：謝。
lines.en: Back in bed, she writes one wobbly character on the board: thanks.

lines.zh: 第二次坐起，她的眼睛開始慌，雙手亂抓床單。沒有人約定過停止手勢。
lines.en: On the second sit her eyes panic and her hands grab at the sheet. No one ever agreed a stop signal.

lines.zh: 躺回去。她不是不行，是沒有人問她怕什麼。
lines.en: Back down. It's not that she can't; nobody asked what she was afraid of.

lines.zh: 明天先談，再坐。清醒的病人要先點頭，身體才會跟。
lines.en: Tomorrow we talk first, then sit. An awake patient nods first; the body follows.

note.zh: 回家的樓梯、日記、加護病房後症候群
note.en: Stairs at home, the diary, post-intensive care syndrome

sub.zh: 我在門口，可以進來了嗎？
sub.en: I'm at the door. May I come in now?

lines.zh: 她什麼時候可以說話？家裡二樓才有廁所，十六階。
lines.en: When will she speak? Our only toilet is upstairs. Sixteen steps.

lines.zh: 說話要等氣切換成可以說話的管子，重症團隊會看時機。樓梯是我們的事。先談疲倦和環境。
lines.en: Speech waits for a speaking tube on the tracheostomy; the intensive-care team will judge the timing. The stairs are ours. Fatigue and environment first.

post.zh: 加護病房肌無力會跟著她回家，加護病房後症候群也會：虛弱、記憶、惡夢。復健從今天就是為了那十六階。
post.en: ICU-acquired weakness will follow her home, and so will post-intensive care syndrome: weakness, memory, nightmares. Today's rehab is already about those sixteen steps.

lines.zh: 這本是她的日記。我每天念給她聽，她聽不聽得到？
lines.en: This is her diary. I read it to her every day. Can she hear it?

lines.zh: 聽得到。而且換您寫：今天她坐起來了，幾點、誰在、她寫了什麼。這叫加護病房日記，出院後她會想讀。
lines.en: She can. And now you write in it: today she sat up, what time, who was there, what she wrote. That is an ICU diary; after discharge she will want to read it.

lines.zh: 我字很醜。
lines.en: My handwriting is terrible.

lines.zh: 她的「謝」也很醜。配得剛好。
lines.en: Her “thanks” was terrible too. A perfect match.

note.zh: 交班：坐了幾分鐘、掉了幾次、誰知道停止手勢
note.en: Handover: minutes sat, drops, who knows the stop signal

guide.en: Hand over at the goal board

lines.zh: 7 床：床緣坐起，血氧掉一次、抽痰後恢復；停止手勢是舉手；晚上請讓她戴眼鏡、開小燈。
lines.en: Bed 7: sat on the edge of the bed, one desaturation resolved after suction; stop signal is a raised hand; glasses on and a small light tonight, please.

lines.zh: 我把「舉手就停」寫在目標板上了。夜班看得到。
lines.en: I've written “hand up means stop” on the goal board. Nights will see it.

lines.zh: 今天三件事：篩檢是讓每個人知道自己的位置；說不出不代表聽不懂；數字掉的時候先看人、看管路。
lines.en: Three things today: the screen is so everyone knows their place; voiceless is not mindless; when the number drops, look at the person and the tubing first.

lines.zh: 早期活動不是勇敢，是準備。
lines.en: Early mobilisation is not bravery. It is preparation.

lines.zh: 他走出加護病房，從櫃子上拿起咖啡。涼的。他還是喝了一口。
lines.en: He steps out of the ICU and picks up the coffee from the cabinet. Cold. He drinks a mouthful anyway.

note.zh: 夜裡拔管路：先找原因，再談約束
note.en: Pulling at lines at night: causes before restraints

sub.zh: 7 床躁動想拔管路，要不要約束？
sub.en: Bed 7 agitated and pulling at lines: restraints?

lines.zh: 7 床晚上開始躁動，一直要抓氣切。夜班問要不要約束。
lines.en: Bed 7 became agitated this evening and keeps reaching for the tracheostomy. Nights are asking about restraints.

lines.zh: 先找譫妄的原因：痛嗎、尿脹嗎、血氧好嗎、哪種藥剛加的。眼鏡戴上、開小燈、告訴她現在幾點在哪裡。
lines.en: Look for the delirium causes first: pain, a full bladder, saturation, any drug just added. Glasses on, a small light, tell her the time and where she is.

lines.zh: 請她先生錄一段聲音放給她聽。約束是最後手段，要醫囑、要時限，請重症醫師決定。
lines.en: Ask her husband to record a message to play to her. Restraints are the last resort, with an order and a time limit; that is the intensivist's call.

lines.zh: 複誦：先找原因、眼鏡小燈報時、先生的聲音、約束最後且由重症醫師決定。
lines.en: Read-back: causes first, glasses, light and the time, the husband's voice, restraints last and the intensivist decides.

lines.zh: 她剛剛舉手了。我們停下來問她，她在白板寫：「想喝水」。
lines.en: She just raised her hand. We stopped and asked; she wrote on the board: “thirsty”.

lines.zh: 你放下電話。目標板旁邊那個歪歪的「謝」，在小燈下還看得到。
lines.en: You put the phone down. Beside the goal board, under the small light, the wobbly “thanks” is still visible.

sub.zh: 早期活動不是勇敢，是準備
sub.en: Early mobilisation is not bravery; it is preparation
